audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty stands; the phase reasoning was generic and unnamed.
audit.why: 54.02% over 733 games and a 6/10 rating fit a lane Olaf owns until Gragas's ultimate exists. Body Slam (14/13.5/13/12.5/12s) is the one stun and Explosive Cask (100/85/70s) is the one escape.
audit.corrected: Kept FAV / 6/10, re-anchored the phases to Body Slam's and Explosive Cask's real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the packet and with the mirror.
audit.why: The mirror (gragas__olaf) already moved win[0] to Olaf, win[2] to Skill, win[3] to Olaf and win[4] to Gragas with the sides to match — identical to the packet chart, and identical to what this entry's own whys already say.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 4 flipped as one atomic group in both layers, ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings credit Gragas with 'Q-pool sustain' — healing from standing in his Q.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is damage plus a slow, nothing else. Gragas's healing is Happy Hour, a PASSIVE that triggers periodically when he uses a skill — so his sustain is paced by his casts and his mana, not by a pool you can walk out of.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed at Happy Hour and its per-cast trigger.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'E true damage ignores his W damage reduction'.
audit.why: True damage ignores armour and magic resist. Drunken Rage reduces damage RECEIVED, which is a different mechanic and still applies — so the advice to swing into an active W was backwards.
audit.corrected: Restated as ignoring armour, with Drunken Rage named as the thing to trade around.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings assert Explosive Cask displaces you 'through Ragnarok' / 'even while Ragnarok makes you CC-immune'.
audit.why: Riot's Ragnarok text says immunity to disables while he keeps attacking, and says nothing about displacement. That is exactly the class of fact the kit files do not settle, so asserting it either way is a guess.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to state only what is verifiable — Explosive Cask is a 100/85/70s knockback and his one escape — with no claim about whether Ragnarok stops it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings give Olaf's W omnivamp/sustain.
audit.why: Tough It Out is attack speed plus a shield; the lifesteal is the passive and scales with missing health.
audit.corrected: Reassigned to the missing-health passive throughout.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Undertow's slow into an auto wins first contact — Gragas has no level-1 burst, and Happy Hour only heals off his casts.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Respect Gragas's Body Slam completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Undertow's slow and Tough It Out's shield win the first trades. Respect Body Slam's 14s stun — these levels are about banking small leads, not proving a point.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Gragas, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.after: Your axe-reset perma-slow and missing-health lifesteal out-grind Happy Hour's per-cast healing in short trades.

edits.after: Explosive Cask is his one out — a 100s knockback that boops you off him or into his jungler, so he owns the level-6 all-in if you dive it blind.

edits.after: Undertow into a Reckless Swing tap out-trades Happy Hour's per-cast healing before he can stack it — your peak window.

edits.after: Force short trades where missing-health lifesteal out-paces Happy Hour and Reckless Swing ignores his armour

edits.before: Gragas wants to chip you with Q and heal it on the pool, but his Q-pool sustain can't keep up with how hard you punish a melee. Land your axe through him for the slow, then walk in for an auto and E true damage — that guaranteed chunk ignores his W damage reduction and out-trades anything his pool heals back. Chase the axe pickup so your Q refunds and the slow never drops, which is what stops him body-slamming away clean. Don't whiff the axe into minions and don't trade into his Q when it's about to come off cooldown.
edits.after: Gragas wants to chip you with Barrel Roll and heal it back with Happy Hour, which only fires when he casts — so his sustain is paced by his mana, not by your damage. Land the axe through him for the slow, then walk in for an auto and Reckless Swing: the true damage ignores his armour, but Drunken Rage still cuts what lands, so swing when that is off. Chase the pickup so Undertow refunds and the slow never drops — that is what stops him Body Slamming away clean. Don't whiff the axe into the minions.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you out-trade him on axe-reset slows and W-omnivamp — every time he steps up to Q-poke you, run him down on the slow before his E is back. Level 6 is the one window where he gets a real answer: his R can knock you off him even while Ragnarok makes you CC-immune, or boop you straight into his jungler, so respect the Flash-R cancel before you commit a dive. Bait the R or wait for it down, then ult and E him out before his pool can save the trade.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you out-trade him on axe-reset slows and missing-health lifesteal — every time he steps up to Barrel Roll, run him down on the slow before Body Slam's 14s is back. Level 6 is the one window where he gets a real answer: Explosive Cask boops you off him or straight into his jungler, so bait it or wait it out before you commit a dive. Then ult, Reckless Swing him out, and Happy Hour will not save the trade.

notes: The 'Q-pool sustain' story ran through six strings and changed the advice: it implied Gragas heals by standing in his Q, so the reader would try to walk him out of it. Happy Hour is a passive on skill use — the counterplay is his mana and anti-heal timing, not the puddle. Two strings also asserted Explosive Cask displaces through Ragnarok; Riot's text does not settle displacement versus disable immunity, so those claims are removed rather than reversed. Listed in unverified. phases[2].rating and phases[3].rating are left as they are (5/10 and 6/10) — they already read correctly for the flipped sides.
